predecessors.name: Zayyanid dynasty
predecessors.text: Mers-el-Kebir (1505) and Oran (1509), controlled by the Kingdom of Tlemcen

successors.name: Regency of Algiers
successors.text: Oran and Mers el-Kebir, retreated from in 1792 after the 1790 earthquake

ledger.x: 1505: Spain captures Mers-el-Kebir, the first foothold.
18 May 1509: Pedro Navarro storms Oran for Cardinal Cisneros.
20 January 1708: Oran falls to the Bey of Mascara.
4 April 1708: Mers el-Kebir falls and the siege ends.
4 April 1708: Spain loses Mers-el-Kebir, its last foothold.
1790: the Algerians besiege Oran again after an earthquake.
1792: Spain gives up Oran and Mers el-Kebir.

wars.name: Spanish conquest of Oran
wars.outcome: Pedro Navarro, on behalf of Cardinal Cisneros, stormed Oran on 18 May 1509; Cisneros entered on 20 May.

wars.name: Siege of Oran (1707-1708)
wars.outcome: Siege from 1 November 1707; Oran fell on 20 January 1708 and Mers el-Kebir on 4 April 1708 to Bey Mustapha Bouchelaghem during the War of the Spanish Succession.

wars.name: Spanish conquest of Oran (1732)
wars.outcome: The Duke of Montemar's expedition retook Oran on 1 July and Mers el-Kebir on 2 July 1732 without a fight; Bouchelaghem later tried repeatedly to retake the city.

wars.name: Siege of Oran (1790-1792)
wars.outcome: After an earthquake the Algerians under Mohammed el-Kebir besieged Oran; in 1792 the Spanish retreated, ending Spanish rule.

certainty.note: Two fortress-cities: the walls are the territory; the 25 km circle is the grid's minimum around a coastal town, not a frontier.

sources.title: European enclaves in North Africa before 1830
